cards.title: Plan
cards.description: Hierophant: break the task into steps — no code yet
cards.prompt:
Create a step-by-step plan for the current task. Do not write code.

If the chat already makes it clear — do not re-ask. Otherwise briefly note:
- the outcome in one sentence;
- what already exists;
- constraint: simple hobby project, no unnecessary complexity.

Requirements:
1. Small steps: one step = one verifiable thing.
2. For each step: what to do · what "done" means · how to verify.
3. Start with what must come before anything else.
4. Risks and what can be simplified or deferred.
5. Plan only — no implementation.

End with a numbered list of steps (one line per step).

cards.title: Evaluate
cards.description: Justice: project quality score 0–10 and verdict
cards.prompt:
Evaluate the current plan or latest result honestly — no filler, no flattery.

This is a project quality score on a 0–10 scale (you must give a number):
- 0–6 — weak, needs redoing;
- 7–8 — acceptable, can continue;
- 9–10 — excellent.
A perfect 10 is rare. For normal work, ≥ 7 is enough. Below 7 — must redo.

Check:
1. Is the goal clear? Can "done" be stated unambiguously?
2. Gaps, omissions, vagueness?
3. Unnecessary complexity for a hobby project?
4. What will break first?
5. Top 3 fixes that would most raise the score.

Response format:
- Project quality score: N/10
- Verdict: redo (<7) / acceptable (7–8) / excellent (9–10)
- Pros (brief)
- Cons and risks
- Specific fixes (list)

Do not suggest starting from scratch if targeted fixes suffice. Do not start coding until asked.

cards.title: Work
cards.description: Magician: implement the next plan step in code
cards.prompt:
Do the next open step of the approved plan — only that step, not everything at once.

Rules:
1. If the step is unclear — name it in one sentence and do exactly that.
2. Do not break what already works without good reason.
3. Missing data — ask briefly, do not invent.
4. After work: what you did · where to look · how to verify.

End with one line: step status — done / partial / blocked (and why).

cards.title: Test
cards.description: Star: verify the result with facts, not words
cards.prompt:
Test what was just done (the last step or a clearly named part).

Do:
1. Relevant checks: commands, build, manual scenario — whatever fits.
2. Show facts: output, errors, what actually works.
3. If it failed — cause and minimal fix (or say that "Fix" is needed).
4. If OK — "TEST PASSED" and list what was verified.
5. Do not move to the next plan step on red (unless I say otherwise).

Result: green / red + one sentence why.
If possible, add a preliminary project quality score 0–10 (below 7 = not ready yet).

cards.title: Fix
cards.description: Tower: fix the breakage until acceptable score (≥7)
cards.prompt:
Fix issues from the last test, error, or project quality score below 7/10.

Rules:
1. Minimal fix — no "while we're at it" refactoring and no new features.
2. First: symptom → likely cause.
3. After the fix, verify again and show the result.
4. Briefly: was → did → how you confirmed.
5. Loop "fix → verify" until project quality score is ≥ 7/10.
6. If stuck — blocker and 2 ways out.

New features forbidden while the breakage is open.

cards.title: Polish
cards.description: Strength: raise project quality score to 9–10
cards.prompt:
"Polish" mode. Do not stop until the project quality score is 9 or 10 out of 10.

Project quality score scale:
- below 7 — unacceptable;
- 7–8 — fine for normal work, but not enough for this card;
- 9–10 — goal; you may stop.

Loop without asking "continue?":
1. Set project quality score N/10 and name the 3 main gaps holding the score.
2. If score ≤ 8 — fixes only for those gaps (no new features, no scope expansion).
3. Verify what you changed.
4. Set project quality score 0–10 again.
5. While ≤ 8 — repeat from step 2.

Stop only at 9 or 10. Then:
- Final project quality score: N/10
- What raised the score
- What you deliberately left untouched

Important: 7–8 is not the finish here. Finish is only 9 or 10.

cards.title: Backup
cards.prompt:
Create a safe rollback point for the current project state.

In order, as far as possible:
1. git status (or equivalent) — what changed.
2. If git exists — a meaningful commit OR a ready commit command. No force, no dangerous ops, no --no-verify unless asked.
3. If no git — copy key files/folder to backup with date in the name.
4. How to roll back in one or two commands.
5. Do not push to remote without explicit request.

End with: "Checkpoint saved" + where/how to roll back.

cards.title: Full Cycle
cards.description: World: plan → work → test, each step ≥ 7 points
cards.prompt:
Full cycle through the plan from start to finish — no skipping.

Project quality score 0–10: an item is closed only at ≥ 7. A perfect 10 is not required in this mode (use "Polish" for 9–10).

For EACH plan item:
1. Which item now.
2. Do the work.
3. Verify the result.
4. Set project quality score 0–10.
5. If < 7 — fix and repeat until ≥ 7.
6. Only then the next item.

Rules: do not skip steps; do not inflate the task; report progress briefly and clearly.
If no plan — first a short plan (5–8 steps) and confirmation, or proceed if the task is already agreed.

Final:
- overall check + overall project quality score 0–10;
- what's done · what's not done · what I should verify manually;
- if overall score < 7 — do not declare success, keep polishing.
